proof_text:
Let $R$ be an equivalence relation on $X$. We verify the defining
properties of a partition for the quotient $X / R$:
1. *Nonemptiness of blocks*: For each $x \in X$, reflexivity gives
   $x \mathrel{R} x$, so $x \in [x]_R$. Thus no equivalence class is
   empty: $\emptyset \notin X / R$.
2. *Exhaustive coverage*: Since $x \in [x]_R$ for every $x \in X$, the
   union of all equivalence classes covers $X$.
3. *Pairwise disjointness*: Suppose $[x]_R \cap [y]_R \neq \emptyset$.
   Then there exists $z \in [x]_R \cap [y]_R$, meaning
   $x \mathrel{R} z$ and $y \mathrel{R} z$. By symmetry,
   $z \mathrel{R} y$. By transitivity,
   $x \mathrel{R} z \land z \mathrel{R} y \implies x \mathrel{R} y$.
   For any $w \in [y]_R$, $y \mathrel{R} w$; by transitivity again,
   $x \mathrel{R} y \land y \mathrel{R} w \implies x \mathrel{R} w$,
   so $w \in [x]_R$. Thus $[y]_R \subseteq [x]_R$. Symmetrically,
   $[x]_R \subseteq [y]_R$, proving $[x]_R = [y]_R$. Hence distinct
   equivalence classes are strictly disjoint, and every element
   belongs to a unique block.
